title: Indexable PII Catalog & Differential Retention for Observability Streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build an indexable PII catalog and implement differential retention tiers for observability telemetry (traces, logs, and metrics) so teams can query and manage sensitive fields without compromising SLO debugging workflows. This ticket covers schema discovery, runtime tagging via tracing hooks, enrichment for a PII index, pipeline enforcement of field-level redaction or pseudonymization, and retention automation based on query patterns and owner policies.
acceptance_criteria: Automated scanner identifies candidate PII fields for new telemetry sources and writes entries to the PII catalog with sampling evidence and owner suggestion.
Tracing instrumentation can attach a PII tag set to spans at the point of generation (SDK hook) and propagate through downstream processors.
Ingest pipeline can apply field-level transformations (none/pseudonymize/hash/redact) driven by catalog rules, with observable metrics for transformed rate.
Retention tiering implemented (hot: 30d, warm: 90d, cold: 365d) and enforced in storage layer per-stream or per-field as policy labels.
RBAC-enabled query audit logs capture who queried sensitive fields, including sampled query text and result cardinality for privacy review.
Dashboard filter that shows 'sensitivity surface' by service: percent of telemetry with PII tags, retention tier distribution, and transformation coverage.
E2E tests that simulate a service emitting a PII field and validate tagging, pipeline transform, storage TTL, and audit-log entry on a read.
Performance impact <6% p50 latency increase on the observability ingest path at 99th percentile load for a typical tenant profile.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Discovery & Catalog: build lightweight scanner job that samples recent logs/traces/metrics and extracts candidate keys/values with heuristics + example regexes. Store catalog entries in a read-optimized catalog service with metadata: field path, evidence, suggested transform, suggested owner.
Phase 2 - Tracing Hooks & SDK: add SDK hook to annotate spans and log envelopes with catalog IDs or sensitivity tags; provide opt-in flags for application teams.

Phase 3 - Pipeline Enforcement: extend pipeline processors to consult catalog rules and apply per-field transform plugins (pseudonymize/hmac, tokenization reference, full redaction). Emit metrics: transformed_count, skipped_count, error_count.

Phase 4 - Retention Automation: assign TTL labels to streams/fields and implement enforcement at the storage tier (S3 lifecycle or DB TTL); provide backfill job to reclassify existing data into new tiers.
Phase 5 - RBAC & Audit: add query-layer instrumentation to log accesses to sensitive catalog IDs, wire logs to an immutable audit stream with tenant and actor metadata.
Phase 6 - Dashboard & Alerts: create dashboards showing PII coverage and retention anomalies; alert when transformation coverage <90% or unexpected retention extension occurs.
Phase 7 - Rollout & Documentation: gradual rollout to a pilot group, run privacy review, publish runbook and run a tabletop incident exercise.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Deploy catalog service and scanner in dry-run mode (no enforcement). Share initial findings with owners and PM.
Week 2-3: Release SDK tracing hook as flag-gated beta for 3 internal services (console, runtime-agent, ingest-proxy). Collect telemetry on tag propagation.
Week 4: Enable pipeline pseudonymization for pilot streams with canary sample rate 5% -> 25% -> 100% if metrics stable.
Week 5: Turn on retention TTL enforcement for pilot non-customer-facing streams; expand as owners sign off.
Week 6: Enable query auditing in read-only mode for 14 days, then enforce and integrate alerts with security team.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for catalog rule matching and transform plugin behavior.
Load test the ingest pipeline with synthetic payloads containing high cardinality PII fields to measure latency impact and memory usage.
Chaos test: simulate transform plugin failures and verify pipeline fallback (drop, passthrough, fail-open behavior per policy).
Privacy verification: run sample re-identification checks on pseudonymized outputs and document K-anonymity estimates for common fields.
Audit validation: assert that every read of a sensitive catalog ID generates an audit entry and that entries are immutable for 90d.
open_questions: What is the canonical owner assignment workflow for a discovered PII field? (self-assign via UI vs automated suggestion + human confirm)
Do we require strong cryptographic guarantees (HSM/KMS-backed tokenization) for some customers, or will HMAC-based pseudonymization suffice initially?
How do we represent compound PII (e.g., device_id + session_id) that is not sensitive alone but together can reidentify?
Should retention tiers be configurable per-customer or enforced globally with overrides?
What SLAs do product teams expect for rehydrating cold data during incident debug?
decisions: Initial approach: implement catalog + transform plugins with HMAC pseudonymization by default; escalate to KMS tokenization for customers that opt-in.
Retention tiers: default hot=30d, warm=90d, cold=365d; make per-stream overrides allowed with security approval.
Audit log storage: use append-only write path to internal audit S3 bucket with lifecycle 3 years and retention controls for compliance teams.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False-positives in scanner cause unnecessary redaction and break debug flows. Mitigation: start in dry-run, provide clear owner review UI and easy opt-out.
Risk: Transform plugins increase ingest latency. Mitigation: implement async path for heavy transforms and measure end-to-end impact; add batch crypto ops.
Risk: Query auditing volume could be very large. Mitigation: sampling policy + aggregated metrics for dashboards and on-demand full-audit exports.
